deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847), which was published posthumously in the Werke (1876). Riemann defines derivatives of arbitrary order ν through a generalized Taylor expansion

z(x+h) = Σ_ν ∂_x^ν z · h^ν/Π(ν),

where Π(ν) = Γ(ν+1) (Gauss's notation) and ν runs through ν0 + ℤ. The red marginal corrections replace an earlier Fraktur 𝔇 by ∂ throughout.

(1) The restriction (completing the sentence from the previous page). ∂^ν z is not to be the coefficient of h^ν/Π(ν) in every possible expansion of z(x+h). It is to be the coefficient only in expansions where the coefficient of h^{ν+1}/Π(ν+1) is the x-derivative of the coefficient of h^ν/Π(ν). Writing p_ν for the coefficient of h^ν/Π(ν), the requirement is p_{ν+1} = d p_ν/dx for every ν.

(2) Claim: a given value of ∂^ν z can belong to only one such expansion.

Proof begun on this page and finished on the next:
- Suppose p_ν belongs to two admissible expansions (a) and (b).
- All later terms p_{ν+1}, p_{ν+2}, … are obtained from p_ν by differentiation, so (a) and (b) agree in all of them.
- Call the earlier terms p_{ν-1}, p_{ν-2}, … in (a) and q_{ν-1}, q_{ν-2}, … in (b). Then p_{ν-1} and q_{ν-1} both have derivative p_ν.
- Next page: hence q_{ν-1} = p_{ν-1} + K1. Integrating again (my filling of the step), q_{ν-2} = p_{ν-2} + K1·x + K2, and q_{ν-3} = p_{ν-3} + K1·x²/2! + K2·x + K3.
- In general (mine), q_{ν-k} = p_{ν-k} + Σ_{m=1}^{k} K_m x^{k-m}/(k-m)!.
- Therefore b − a = Σ_m K_m Σ_{n≥0} x^n/n! · h^{ν-m-n}/Π(ν-m-n) = Σ_m K_m (x+h)^{ν-m}/Π(ν-m), by the generalized binomial series (valid for |x| < |h|).
- Since a = b must hold for all values of x+h, all K_m = 0, and the two expansions coincide.

(3) Footnote *). The law (4) (presumably the composition law for ∂) gives two facts:
- Σ ∂^ν z · h^ν/Π(ν) is an expansion of z(x+h);
- Σ (d ∂^ν z/dx) · h^{ν+1}/Π(ν+1) is also an expansion of z(x+h).
It does not give that these two expansions are identical. This explains why the restriction in (1) is imposed as an additional postulate. The red margin note says 'Als Note unter den Text' (to be set as a footnote).
errors: No error on this page. The argument is unfinished here; the key step that p_{ν-1} and q_{ν-1} differ only by a constant is on the next page.

Implicit assumption: the expansion runs over infinitely many lower orders ν-1, ν-2, …. The rearrangement into Σ K_m (x+h)^{ν-m}/Π(ν-m) needs convergence (|x|<|h|) and interchange of a double infinite sum, neither of which is justified.

The conclusion that all K_m = 0 (next page, 'bekanntlich') needs the linear independence of the infinitely many functions (x+h)^{ν-m} under convergent infinite sums. This is plausible, but no proof is given.
Riemann's broader theory is known to suffer from the ambiguity of the 'complementary function' (discussed later, e.g. by Cayley 1880). Here that ambiguity is handled only by postulate.

results.what: Definition of fractional derivatives as coefficients of a generalized Taylor series z(x+h)=Σ ∂^ν z h^ν/Γ(ν+1), with the compatibility condition p_{ν+1}=dp_ν/dx
results.modern_name: Riemann's generalized Taylor series / Riemann approach to fractional calculus (precursor of the Riemann–Liouville integral)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1847 student essay, publ. 1876 in Werke); Liouville (1832) for earlier fractional calculus

results.what: Uniqueness: a given ∂^ν z determines at most one admissible expansion; differences are Σ K_m (x+h)^{ν-m}/Γ(ν-m+1)
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of the generalized Taylor expansion modulo the complementary function

results.what: Generalized binomial resummation Σ_n x^n/n! · h^{a-n}/Γ(a-n+1) = (x+h)^a/Γ(a+1)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of Riemann's 1847 essay on generalized differentiation, which was published in his collected Werke (1876) and is well known in the history of fractional calculus. The content matches the published text.

checkable.asserts: The coefficient system h^ν/Π(ν) is compatible with differentiation: d/dx of x^a/Γ(a+1) equals x^(a-1)/Γ(a); should give 0.
Generalized binomial resummation Σ x^n/n! h^{a-n}/Γ(a-n+1) = (x+h)^a/Γ(a+1) at a=1/2, x=0.3, h=1; should be ≈ 0.

checkable.sympy: x,K1,K2,K3=symbols('x K1 K2 K3'); d1=K1; d2=K1*x+K2; d3=K1*x**2/2+K2*x+K3; [simplify(diff(d2,x)-d1), simplify(diff(d3,x)-d2)]
checkable.asserts: The successive differences q_{ν-k}-p_{ν-k} are consistent with q' = q_{previous}; should give [0, 0].

transcription_corrections: 'daß ein Werth von [-∂^ν z-] aus einer Entwicklung angehören kann' should read 'daß ein Werth von ∂^ν z nur einer Entwicklung angehören kann' ('ein' is underlined for emphasis). The symbol is not struck through; it was redrawn as ∂ in the red margin correction.
'ein Werth von [-∂z-], p_ν' should read 'ein Werth von ∂^ν z, p_ν'.
'p_ν entstehen' — the subscript ν is written under the p ('aus p_ν entstehen').
'z x+h' in the footnote should read 'z(x+h)'.
'beide zum Differential p_ν' continues on the next page with '…haben'.
The red margin text 'Als Note unter den Text.' refers to the bracketed passage marked *) being set as a footnote. The repeated red marginal symbols are corrections of Fraktur 𝔇_x^ν z to ∂_x^ν z.
